schema_note: Data-driven pharmacology. Each substance has PK (one-compartment: absorption_min + elimination half_life_min via a gut->blood model) and PD `effects`: the approximate STEADY-STATE shift each shared BodyState variable takes at ONE standard dose (in the variable's own units — bpm, mmHg, ug/dL cortisol, 0-1 alertness). The engine converts these to the right dynamics and scales by actual dose and blood level, so effects rise and fade with the drug. Add a new drug/substance HERE — no code change — so the simulator can address 'what does X do to me' for substances it was never explicitly built for. Coefficients are directional/approximate, graded WEAK-to-MODERATE, and are NOT medical advice.

nicotine.note: Stimulant; raises heart rate and blood pressure, transiently increases alertness and cortisol.

melatonin.note: Sleep-timing hormone; reduces alertness (promotes sleep onset) and mildly lowers heart rate.

pseudoephedrine.note: Decongestant sympathomimetic; raises blood pressure and heart rate, mildly stimulating.

l_theanine.note: Calming amino acid; slightly lowers heart rate/BP and blunts the stress response (often paired with caffeine).

diphenhydramine.note: Sedating antihistamine; strongly reduces alertness/causes drowsiness (mild anticholinergic tachycardia).
